note: Rewritten from the original English description by Sands (1959); the original is in English; in the scan many of the decimal points and range marks of the measurements are read as colons and semicolons (e.g. "0: 87-1 + 02"), and this entry restores them to 0.87—1.02 according to the upper, lower and mean columns, adopting only the ranges and not the means; population differences left unquantified in the original, such as "East African alates very slightly larger than the type", are omitted as such.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate has a short but distinct emarginate median lobe on the anterior margin of the pronotum, a form not seen in any other species of the genus in the Ethiopian region, including Amitermes hastatus, which resembles it in the soldier. The anterior surface of the fore coxa of the soldier bears 1—4 spines in the middle, shared with A. unidentatus, A. acinacifer, A. acutidens and A. curvatus, the last three usually smaller. A. harleyi, described by Harris in 1957, agrees with specimens from northern Kenya and is treated as a synonym of this species; A. hastatus as recorded by Sjöstedt from Mount Kilimanjaro is also referred here.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Colour: head and pronotum deep sepia brown, postclypeus only slightly paler, brown; antennae pale brown, the apex of each segment yellowish white; labrum pale yellow; thoracic sclerites (except the pronotum), abdominal tergites and the sides of the sternites sepia brown; femora pale, tibiae dark at the base and gradually paler towards the apex, tarsi pale yellowish white; middle of the abdominal sternites yellowish white; wings semi-transparent pale brown, the veins throughout sepia brown. Posterior margin of the head almost semicircular; fontanelle pale, broadly oval, about as large as an ocellus, slightly concave, in front of it a narrow, parallel-sided pale extension almost as long as the rest of the fontanelle; eye as long as or slightly shorter than the postclypeus; ocelli moderate, the distance to the eye slightly greater than the width of an ocellus; postclypeus inflated, about half as long as wide, posterior margin convex, arched in the middle, sides fairly straight, anterior margin straight; antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 about half of segment 2, segments 4 and 5 subequal, shorter than segment 2 and longer than segment 3. Pronotum distinctly narrower than the head width including eyes, the anterior margin produced in the middle into a short but distinct emarginate lobe, the sides broadly rounded, narrowing posteriorly to a slightly concave posterior margin. Entire body covered with fine, short, pale hairs; the hairs of the abdominal intersegmental membranes shorter, curved and yellow. Male similar to female, but the wings usually slightly smaller. Measurements (mm): head width including eyes 0.87—1.02; maximum diameter of eye 0.21—0.26; ocelli 0.06—0.07 × 0.09—0.10; ocellus to eye 0.07—0.08; pronotum width 0.72—0.86, length 0.47—0.57; hind tibia length 0.89—1.04; forewing length 8.80—10.50.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Colour: head capsule mainly pale yellow, sometimes yellowish brown to reddish brown at the sides and in front of the fontanelle; mandibles yellowish brown to deep reddish brown; antennae, pronotum and legs yellow, the anterior part of the pronotum sometimes slightly darker; the rest yellowish white, the abdomen taking colour from the gut contents. Head in dorsal view distinctly longer than wide, the outline variable, somewhat rounded-rectangular, the posterior margin sometimes evenly rounded; in lateral view continuously curved from the fontanelle to the occiput, the anterior curvature shallower. Mandibles slightly more than half the head length, slender, strongly hooked; the tooth near the middle, directed straight backwards and continuous with the inner margin in front of it, not projecting; the inner margin from the tooth to the apex a regular arc. Antennae normally 14-segmented, segment 2 equal to segments 3 and 4 together, segment 5 longer than segments 3 and 4 but shorter than segment 2. Head capsule with scattered, fairly long setae, denser near the fontanelle. Anterior margin of the pronotum entire or slightly concave. Legs sparsely covered with short hairs; the anterior surface of the fore coxa with 1—4 spines in a group in the middle. Measurements (mm): head length 1.02—1.55; maximum head width 0.78—1.18; head width at the mandible base 0.64—0.89; head thickness 0.68—1.00; left mandible length 0.65—0.86; pronotum length 0.32—0.43, width 0.54—0.74; hind tibia length 0.68—0.93.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Body yellowish white. The third marginal tooth of the left mandible has no clear boundary with the cutting edge between it and the first marginal tooth. The fore coxa bears spines, as in the soldier; this distinguishes it from Amitermes unidentatus, with which it is among the commonest species at many localities.
